text:
Anya: Heads-up — after flipping FP8+INT8 hybrid kernels on the staging fleet I see a reproducible throughput regression for long-context runs where the KV cache is hot. Batch=8, seq=4096 workload, model variant=redwood-3b-32k-quant. Baseline INT8 path: 120 tps. Hybrid FP8 path: 98 tps (≈-18%). p50 latency +12%.

Michael: Do you have a flamegraph/profile? My first guess is we're hitting a routing fallback per-token or extra memcpy when the KV cache is touched.

Anya: Pasting the two quick traces I ran (simplified):
```
-- profile int8 baseline (batch=8, seq=4096) --
kernel_dispatch: 42%
attention_kv_read: 18%
softmax: 6%
memcpy_d2d: 4%
others: 30%

-- profile fp8 hybrid (same config) --
kernel_dispatch: 51%  <-- extra decision work
attention_kv_read: 17%
softmax: 6%
memcpy_d2d: 9%  <-- doubled memcpy
others: 17%
```

Sam: Hmm that memcpy jump is suspicious. Are we serializing/unpacking FP8 tensors per-layer when KV cache is used? Could be a conversion path that triggers on cached keys.

Ravi: @Anya can you dump the kernel selection logs? We added an implicit "safe-fallback" when kv_active==true and precision==FP8 to avoid numerical blowups; it should be O(1) check but maybe it's in the hot loop.

Anya: Kernel routing snippet from logs (snip):
```
for each token:
  if (kv_cache_active && kernel_flags.supports_fp8 == false) route_to_fallback();
  else if (seq_len > 2048 && kernel_flags.large_seq_optimized) use_large_seq_kernel();
  else use_default_kernel();
```
Routing_count: default=3.2M, fallback=1.1M, large_seq=0.9M for a single 5000-token run.

Jen: That per-token branching explains the kernel_dispatch blowup. If the check is inside the token loop and touches metadata it will serialize the hot path. Could we hoist the conditions to per-layer / per-request?

Michael: Also check the KV cache memory layout: FP8 packing/unpacking might be happening lazily on first read, causing memcpy spikes across attention heads. If we pack/unpack per-head per-token that's terrible.

Sam: Quick microbenchmark results I ran after instrumenting pack/unpack counters:
- pack/unpack calls per forward: baseline-int8: ~8k calls, fp8-hybrid: ~32k calls
- average memcpy size: 16KB -> 32KB when fallback engaged

Anya: On the quality side: we traced the root cause to calibration. The FP8 scales were computed from a calibration set that included rare sequences with huge activation spikes (logit-whales). Those outliers pushed scales up and made hybrid kernels more conservative in one path while fallback still expects different ranges, so we added extra protection logic.

Ravi: What calibration procedure did we use? Per-tensor or per-channel? Clip threshold?

Anya: We used the default per-tensor symmetric min-max with 99.999 percentile (i.e., only clipped extremely rare values). The dataset we used included several long-code dumps and some synthetic adversarial prompts — small number of examples but extreme values.

Jen: Per-channel usually helps for kernels (esp. QAT-like distributions) but it's more expensive at runtime and increases kernel binaries. There's a tradeoff: per-channel reduces range skew which can reduce those unsafe fallback checks.

Sam: I ran a small experiment:
- per-tensor + 99.999 percentile: perf -18%, PPL (eval) baseline +0.4
- per-channel + 99.999 percentile: perf -6%, PPL +0.5
- per-channel + 99.9 percentile clipping: perf -2% (within noise), PPL +0.6
So per-channel + slightly more aggressive clipping seems to restore perf while keeping quality degradation modest.

Ravi: Nice. We should also consider dataset pruning for calibration: exclude sequences where max activation > mean+12*std or similar outlier filter. That will avoid letting a handful of adversarial examples dominate scales.

Michael: Agree. Operational suggestions:
- move routing checks out of inner token loop (hoist per-request)
- ensure pack/unpack is done once per KV slab, not per-head-per-token
- try per-channel calibration + 99.9 percentile or 99.5 in a staging A/B
- add telemetry on kernel_fallback_count and pack_unwrap_calls per request

ci-bot: Deploy perf-gate job #342: FAILED (throughput drop >10%). See: https://ci/infra/342

Anya: Action list for next 48h:
1) Sam to add hoisting PR for kernel routing (simple refactor).
2) Jen to run per-channel + {99.9,99.5} clipping experiments on our calibration corpus and produce PPL/wer table.
3) Ravi to add post-calibration outlier-filtering step and provide a small script to prune calibration set by activation z-score.
4) Michael to add telemetry metrics (fallback_count, pack_calls, avg_memcpy_bytes) to runtime.

Sam: I'll push the hoist PR in a bit and run microbench on the staging GPU pool. If hoist fixes kernel_dispatch we should regain much of the lost throughput even before re-calibration.

Anya: Thanks all — I've attached a tiny sample of the problematic calibration inputs to the thread (list pasted below) so we can reproduce locally: "<long-shell-log>, <generated adversarial prompt>, <minified js dump>".

Ravi: Good. Once we have telemetry we can roll an auto-fallback policy: if fallback_count per-req > X then route that request to dedicated int8 pool instead of hybrid, while we fix calibration.

Jen: Also note: per-channel increases model size of scale tensors slightly; we should measure memory delta on the smallest Dedicated SKU.

Michael: OK — priorities set. We'll try the hoist first, then per-channel+clip in A/B. If anyone hits a blocker ping me or @platform-oncall. :thumbsup:
